Contract.title: Installed GRACE skills have one owner and a verifiable installation-health state
Contract.Problem: Intervention I-010 records P-017: package refresh and a project mirror generator wrote competing banners into the same installed `grace5-*` directories, so a required check failed and passed on the same candidate after excluded files changed. Installation health and candidate evidence need separate ownership and freshness.
Contract.Change: Installed `grace5-*` skill directories under `.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` become package-owned: a project mirror generator must not rewrite them in a competing format and must continue validating project-owned skills. A dedicated installation-health tool compares every installed `grace5-*` directory with the packaged skill bytes and the state pin, reports drift with the differing paths, writes nothing, and exits nonzero. `upgrade.md`, `source-identity.md`, `grace5-prepare` and `grace5-execute` state that installation health is evaluated afresh at handoff, while a required check that depends on excluded inputs is not candidate evidence unless a bounded dependency fingerprint is separately approved. No fingerprint mechanism is added by this change.

Constraints.Constraint: Installed `grace5-*` directories remain kernel-managed and excluded from the candidate; the health check reads them but writes no source path.
The existing refresh remains the only writer of installed packaged skills; the change adds no automatic project-file write and no new migration boundary.
An installation-health pass never substitutes for a candidate check, an owner approval or a receipt.
One ledger entry is added for the installation-health mechanism with its removal criterion; a dependency fingerprint is not added.
An ordinary change: no version, pin, tag, migration row or release moves.
Project-owned skills and the project's own mirror validation remain outside the installed package-owned directories; the change does not take ownership of them.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No automatic repair or rewrite of installed skills; drift is reported and the existing refresh remains the repair path.
No arbitrary dependency fingerprint, cache hash or hash of all GRACE records. A fingerprint needs its own approved contract if a real required check cannot be separated.
No weakening of a required check and no deletion of an assertion to turn an installation failure green.
No new kernel command, receipt field or migration boundary.
No client-specific mirror-generator implementation inside this framework repository.

Acceptance.Criterion: A clean upgrade followed by project mirror validation reproduces without alternating rewrites, and the project mirror path does not change installed packaged skill bytes.

Corrupting an installed `grace5-*` file makes installation health fail; restoring the exact packaged bytes makes it pass; corrupting a project-owned mirrored skill still fails the existing mirror check.
The health check reports the pin and the differing paths, writes nothing, and treats a missing packaged skill source as an actionable error rather than a pass.
The ownership rule and the handoff-time freshness rule are stated in upgrade, source-identity and lifecycle guidance for every retained required check that depends on excluded inputs.
Generated packages and the CLI reference remain current after the documentation and guidance changes.
The installation-health tool and upgrade code type-check with the rest of the kernel.

Decisions.Decision: Installed packaged skill directories are owned by the package; a project mirror generator validates only project-owned skills and never rewrites those directories.
Installation health is evaluated afresh at handoff and is not candidate evidence; a check result on an earlier candidate never makes an installation pass current.
No dependency fingerprint is introduced by default; it is admitted only by a separate approved contract for a real required check that cannot be separated from installation health.
Drift is reported, not repaired automatically; the existing refresh remains the only writer.
The health tool reads the pin and installed bytes and writes nothing, so it changes no candidate and needs no owner gate of its own.
A failing assertion is never deleted to make the installation green; the ownership conflict is resolved instead.
